label: vllm-dflash-deployed
context:
DGX Spark vLLM deployment with DFlash speculative decoding is COMPLETE and RUNNING.

What was accomplished:
- Option 1 (n-gram speculative): Deployed and tested, ~6.5 tok/s single-stream
- Option 2 (DFlash draft model): Deployed and RUNNING, 18.4 tok/s (2.8x baseline)
  - Target: Qwen3.6-27B-Uncensored
  - Draft: Qwen3.5-27B-DFlash (custom trained via SpecForge)
  - Config: FP8 weights, prefix caching OFF, batch tokens 32768, max seqs 128
  - Quality: No degradation observed
  - Trade-off: KV cache reduced 966K→499K tokens

Key files:
- Deploy script: /tmp/deploy_vllm_dflash.sh
- DFlash model: /data/models/Qwen3.5-27B-DFlash
- LoRA adapter: /data/SpecForge/custom_dflash/checkpoints/final_model/
- Benchmark script: /tmp/bench_vllm.sh

Current state:
- vLLM server is running on DGX Spark with DFlash
- All persistence layers updated (memory, skill, knowledge, SOUL.md)
- Checkpoints created for both Option 1 and Option 2

Next options to explore:
- Option 3: EAGLE-3 speculative decoding (more aggressive, harder to set up)
- Option 4: FP8 KV cache (memory savings, may help batch size)
- Option 5: Qwen3.7 when released

User asked about creating a systemd service file for auto-start on boot.
decisions: Use DFlash as primary speculative decoding method (2.8x speedup, stable)
Disable prefix caching for hybrid Mamba models (0% hit rate)
Keep FP8 weights for memory efficiency
Do NOT use --enable-prefix-caching with Qwen3.6 hybrid Mamba
